content:
After sending, when you look in settings>privacy&security, is the password there? And can you send multiple messages prior to closing down Thunderbird? And, when you restart thunderbird, is the password missing from settings>privacy&security? If the answer is YES, then my guess is the prefs.js file in the profile is being prevented from updating at shutdown. This might be an antivirus or VPN interfering. You can check this by these steps:

  1. click help>troubleshootinginformation
  2. scroll to 'profile folder' and click 'open folder'
  3. you are now in the profile. see if there is more than one prefs.js file (such as prefs-1.js, prefs-2.js). If the dates are current, that is proof of the problem. Although I have no idea what is causing the problem, you can often fix current issue by deleting all copies except the one with highest number, and then renaming that one to prefs.js.

content:
OK, I missed that you already mentioned in your first message Thunderbird not responding. Now please try to start Thunderbird in "troubleshoot mode" : hold down the Shift key while launching Thunderbird. https://support.mozilla.org/en-US/kb/troubleshoot-mode-thunderbird If Thunderbird still doesn't respond, force-quit the application:

Now try to open the Thunderbird profile folder: press the Windows key and start typing %APPDATA%\Thunderbird\Profiles\ This will open the folder "Profiles" in the Windows file explorer. "Profiles" may contain one or several folders: if you see only one folder "xxxxxxxx.default", open it, look for the prefs.js file and retrieve its size. If the size is 6 to 7 kB it happens to be a newly created file which doesn't contain any account settings , and you will have to look for a prefs-1.js (or invalidprefs.js) file with a much bigger size and an actual time stamp. This prefs-1.js (or more general prefs-x.js) file would be the corrupt "old" prefs.js file which has be renamed in prefs-1.js by Thunderbird.

If you see more than one folder in "Profiles", such as xxxxxxxx.default and yyyyyyyy.default-release (or ......default-esr) , then open the ...default-release or the default -esr folder and search for the prefs.js and a prefs-1.js files

content: What is the name of the "missing" provider? Most major email providers (Gmail, Yahoo, Comcast, etc.) now use OAuth2 for account authentication. They no longer leave an actual password in Saved Passwords, rather they leave a "token" that verifies that you have been authenticated on that device. The token appears as a long string of arbitrary characters. Is this what you are seeing? You cannot see the actual password for those accounts in Thunderbird.
